chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, and others, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
It is disliked for the man that he should descend into the grave of his son.

key_terms.يُكْرَهُ: Disliked (makruh, a category of legal ruling)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a father being buried in the same grave as his son in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the *karahah* (dislike) of a father being buried in the same grave as his son, reflecting the Shia jurisprudential preference for distinct burial spaces to maintain individual dignity. This ruling is often contextualized within broader discussions on grave architecture and the prohibition of excessive veneration that might blur the distinction between the deceased and the divine. It underscores the Shia emphasis on modesty in death and the preservation of the individual's spiritual identity in the Barzakh.
